title: Pontificale consecrates the same altar twice—once as sepulcher, once as altar—with distinct forms
source_text: XXIII. Sed quod maxime notandum est, Alia plane ratione, quam qua statuit Bellarminus, altaria Sanctis dedicari docet Pontificale Romanum, qui liber est publica Pontificum Romanorum authoritate sancitus. Etenim in eo libro separatim habetur consecratio altaris, ut sepulchrum quoddam est; & ejusdem ut altare est. Et quidem ut sepulchrum consecratur his verbis, Consecretur & sanctificetur hoc sepulchrum in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti. Cum vero ut altare consecratur, alia sunt verba. Pontificale Parisiensis An. 1615. pag. 229.
pass_a_gloss: But what is most to be noted, the Roman Pontifical—a book sanctioned by the public authority of the Roman Pontiffs—teaches that altars are dedicated to the Saints by a plainly other reason than that which Bellarmine lays down. For in that book the consecration of an altar as it is a certain sepulcher is had separately; and of the same as it is an altar. And indeed as a sepulcher it is consecrated with these words: Let this sepulcher be consecrated and sanctified in the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. But when it is consecrated as an altar, there are other words. Pontifical of Paris, year 1615, page 229.
pass_b_english: The Pontificale splits consecration: sepulcher-form and altar-form for the same stone.
That public rite is not Bellarmino’s tomb-only permission scheme.

choices.why: Public papal liturgical authority vs private School gloss.
